title: One-Step Read of a Boolean Digit
statement: Let $Q$ and $T$ be types with decidable equality, let $x$ be a finite word over the record alphabet determined by $Q$ and $T$, and let $d$ be a four-work-tape configuration of the digit-reading machine on input $x$. If the state of $d$ is the initial state, then after one step the configuration is exactly $d$ with its state replaced by the state that records the optional Boolean decoded from the symbol under the input head (a digit symbol decodes to its Boolean value, and every other symbol decodes to no value). Moreover, at every time $u<1$, the machine's state is not any state of the form that records a Boolean value.
hypotheses_covered: Q and T have decidable equality
x is a finite record-alphabet input word
d is a four-work-tape configuration on x
